root_cause.text: The length validation for ATOMIC_WRITE requests in `check_rkey()` only compared `pktlen` against `resid`, failing to enforce the IBA-specified exact 8-byte payload length, so a zero-length request bypassed the check and reached `atomic_write_reply()`, which unconditionally reads 8 bytes from the packet payload, resulting in an out-of-bounds read into kernel tailroom and remote information disclosure.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description states "check_rkey() previously accepted an ATOMIC_WRITE request with pktlen == resid == 0 because the length validation only compared pktlen against resid." The patch adds a new check in `check_rkey()` for `RXE_ATOMIC_WRITE_MASK` that requires `resid != sizeof(u64) || pktlen != sizeof(u64) || bth_pad(pkt)` to be rejected, explicitly enforcing the 8-byte payload length.
